package.name: @bankkroll/tesdk
package.description: Universal TypeScript SDK for the Tesla Fleet API — runs on Node, browsers, and edge runtimes.

client.name: TeslaClient
client.doc:
Client for the Tesla Fleet API.

Runs unmodified on Node 20+, browsers, Deno, Bun, and edge runtimes. All
network access goes through a single HttpClient, so timeouts,
retries, and authentication behave identically across every namespace.

examples.title: Static token
examples.code:
const client = new TeslaClient({ region: 'na', accessToken: process.env.TESLA_TOKEN })
const vehicles = await client.vehicles.list()

examples.title: Automatic refresh

members.name: forUserRegion
members.doc:
Returns a client bound to the region Tesla assigns to this account.

Requests to the wrong regional host fail, so this resolves the correct one
when it is not known ahead of time.

examples.code: const client = await new TeslaClient({ accessToken }).forUserRegion()

namespaces.blurb: Listing, live data, wake handling, drivers, and share invites.
namespaces.name: VehiclesResource
namespaces.doc:
Vehicle data and lifecycle operations.

Accessed as `client.vehicles`.

members.name: list
members.doc: Lists vehicles on the account.

members.name: listAll
members.doc: Iterates every vehicle on the account, requesting pages lazily.

members.name: get
members.doc:
Retrieves a vehicle summary, including its connectivity state.

Does not wake the vehicle, making it the cheapest way to check whether a
vehicle is reachable.

members.name: data
members.doc:
Fetches a live snapshot from the vehicle.

Tesla treats this endpoint as billable and rate-sensitive; use Fleet
Telemetry for continuous monitoring rather than polling here.
throws: {VehicleAsleepError} When the vehicle is asleep or unreachable.

members.name: wakeUp
members.doc:
Requests that the vehicle wake from sleep.

Returns as soon as the request is accepted; the vehicle typically takes
10 to 60 seconds to report `online`. Use ensureAwake to wait.

members.name: ensureAwake
members.doc:
Wakes the vehicle if needed and resolves once it reports `online`.

Returns immediately when the vehicle is already online, so it is safe to
call before any command.
throws: {TimeoutError} When the vehicle does not wake within `maxWaitMs`.

members.name: withWake
members.signature: withWake<T>(vin: string, operation: () => Promise<T>, options?: EnsureAwakeOptions): Promise<T>
members.doc: Runs an operation, waking the vehicle once and retrying if it was asleep.

members.name: drivers
members.doc:
Returns the drivers permitted to access the vehicle.

Available only to the vehicle owner.

members.name: removeDriver
members.signature: removeDriver(vin: string, shareUserId: number, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Revokes a driver's access to the vehicle.

Share users may remove only their own access; owners may remove any.
params: shareUserId - Identifier from a drivers entry.

members.name: specs
members.doc:
Returns specifications recorded at the time of sale.

Billed at a fixed rate per successful result and accessible only with a
partner token, for any VIN without owner authorization.

members.name: fleetStatus
members.doc:
Reports application-relevant state for up to a batch of VINs.

The authoritative way to discover whether a vehicle requires Vehicle
Command Protocol signing and whether this application's virtual key is
paired, rather than inferring either from model year.
params: vins - VINs to query.

members.name: shareInvites
members.signature: shareInvites(vin: string, options?: PageOptions & RequestOverrides): Promise<ShareInvite[]>
members.doc:
Returns the active share invites for a vehicle.

Paginated with a maximum page size of 25.

members.name: createShareInvite
members.doc:
Creates a single-use share invite that expires after 24 hours.

Grants driver-level app access, which excludes some owner-only features
such as Service and Roadside. Up to five drivers may be added at a time,
and the vehicle need not be online.

Never retried automatically: each call mints a distinct invite link.

members.name: revokeShareInvite
members.signature: revokeShareInvite(vin: string, invitationId: string, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: redeemShareInvite
members.doc: Redeems a share invite, granting the authenticated account app access.
params: code - Single-use code from the invite link.

namespaces.blurb: Every actuating command, from locks to navigation.
namespaces.name: CommandsResource
namespaces.doc:
Remote control commands for a vehicle.

Accessed as `client.commands`.

members.name: send
members.signature: send(vin: string, command: string, body?: Record<string, unknown>, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Sends an arbitrary command, including endpoints newer than this SDK.
params: vin - Vehicle identification number.
command - Command name as it appears in the Fleet API path.
body - JSON body for commands that take parameters.

members.name: signedCommand
members.signature: signedCommand(vin: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Sends a pre-signed command envelope.

The generic endpoint that replaces the individual legacy command routes,
carrying a payload already signed with the Vehicle Command Protocol. Use
it only when signing is handled outside this SDK; a Vehicle Command Proxy
signs the ordinary command methods for you.
params: payload - Signed protocol message.

members.name: honkHorn
members.doc:
Sounds the horn.

Never retried automatically, since a repeat would honk twice.

members.name: setChargeLimit
members.signature: setChargeLimit(vin: string, percent: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Sets the charge limit.
params: percent - Target state of charge, from 50 to 100.

members.name: setChargingAmps
members.signature: setChargingAmps(vin: string, chargingAmps: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Sets the charging current.
params:
chargingAmps - Requested amperage, clamped by the vehicle to what
the connected circuit supports.

members.name: setTemps
members.doc: Sets driver and passenger temperature targets.

members.name: setSeatHeater
members.signature: setSeatHeater(vin: string, seat: SeatPosition, level: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Sets a seat heater level.
params: level - `0` for off through `3` for maximum.

members.name: setSentryMode
members.signature: setSentryMode(vin: string, on: boolean, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: actuateTrunk
members.signature: actuateTrunk(vin: string, which: 'front' | 'rear', options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Actuates the front or rear trunk.

The rear trunk toggles on vehicles with a powered liftgate, so repeated
calls are not idempotent and are never retried.
params: which - `front` for the frunk, `rear` for the trunk.

members.name: windowControl
members.doc:
Vents or closes the windows of a parked vehicle.

Closing requires the user's coordinates so the vehicle can confirm they
are nearby. Model 3 is exempt from that check, which is why the
coordinates are optional.
params:
position - User latitude and longitude, required to close on most
platforms.

members.name: sunRoofControl
members.signature: sunRoofControl(vin: string, state: 'stop' | 'close' | 'vent', options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: setBioweaponMode
members.signature: setBioweaponMode(vin: string, on: boolean, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: setClimateKeeperMode
members.signature: setClimateKeeperMode(vin: string, mode: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Sets Climate Keeper mode.
params: mode - `0` off, `1` Keep, `2` Dog, `3` Camp.

members.name: setValetMode
members.signature: setValetMode(vin: string, on: boolean, password?: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Turns on Valet Mode with a four-digit passcode.
params: password - Four-digit passcode required to exit Valet Mode.

members.name: speedLimitActivate
members.signature: speedLimitActivate(vin: string, pin: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: speedLimitDeactivate
members.signature: speedLimitDeactivate(vin: string, pin: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: speedLimitSetLimit
members.signature: speedLimitSetLimit(vin: string, limitMph: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: mediaTogglePlayback
members.doc:
Toggles media playback.

Media commands are never retried, since a repeat would skip an extra track
or toggle playback back to its previous state.

members.name: adjustVolume
members.signature: adjustVolume(vin: string, volume: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Sets media playback volume.

Requires the user to be present and mobile access to be enabled.
params: volume - Level from 0 to 11.

members.name: navigationSuperchargerRequest
members.signature: navigationSuperchargerRequest(vin: string, id: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: addChargeSchedule
members.signature: addChargeSchedule(vin: string, schedule: Record<string, unknown>, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Adds a charge schedule.

Preferred over `set_scheduled_charging` from firmware 2024.26 onward.
Existing schedules are readable via the `charge_schedule_data` subtree of
VehiclesResource.data.

members.name: removeChargeSchedule
members.signature: removeChargeSchedule(vin: string, id: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: addPreconditionSchedule
members.signature: addPreconditionSchedule(vin: string, schedule: Record<string, unknown>, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: removePreconditionSchedule
members.signature: removePreconditionSchedule(vin: string, id: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: setPinToDrive
members.signature: setPinToDrive(vin: string, pin: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Sets a four-digit PIN to Drive passcode.

Requires Vehicle Command Protocol signing, and is restricted to fleet
managers and owners. The vehicle retains the first PIN it is given, so
changing it requires resetPinToDrive first.

members.name: resetPinToDrive
members.doc:
Clears PIN to Drive.

Requires Vehicle Command Protocol signing, and works only while PIN to
Drive is inactive and the vehicle is not in Valet Mode.

members.name: setGuestMode
members.signature: setGuestMode(vin: string, enable: boolean, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

members.name: remoteBoombox
members.signature: remoteBoombox(vin: string, sound: 0 | 2000, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Plays a sound through the external speaker.
params: sound - `0` for the random fart, `2000` for the locate ping.

members.name: setVehicleName
members.signature: setVehicleName(vin: string, name: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc:
Sets the vehicle name.

Requires Vehicle Command Protocol signing on all supported vehicles.

members.name: navigationRequest
members.signature: navigationRequest(vin: string, value: string, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>
members.doc: Shares a destination, address, or search query with the navigation system.
params: value - An address, a `latitude,longitude` pair, or a share URL.

members.name: scheduleSoftwareUpdate
members.signature: scheduleSoftwareUpdate(vin: string, offsetSeconds: number, options?: SendCommandOptions): Promise<CommandResult>

namespaces.blurb: Powerwall, Solar, and Wall Connector sites.
namespaces.name: EnergyResource
namespaces.doc:
Energy site data and control.

Accessed as `client.energy`.

members.name: products
members.doc: Lists every product on the account, including vehicles and energy sites.

members.name: liveStatus
members.signature: liveStatus(siteId: number | string, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergySiteLiveStatus>

members.name: siteInfo
members.signature: siteInfo(siteId: number | string, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergySiteInfo>

members.name: energyHistory
members.signature: energyHistory(siteId: number | string, period: HistoryPeriod, options?: HistoryRangeOptions): Promise<EnergyHistory>
members.doc:
Returns site energy measurements aggregated to the requested period.

Energy values are in watt-hours.

members.name: backupHistory
members.signature: backupHistory(siteId: number | string, period: HistoryPeriod, options?: HistoryRangeOptions): Promise<EnergyHistory>

members.name: chargeHistory
members.signature: chargeHistory(siteId: number | string, options?: Omit<HistoryRangeOptions, 'period'>): Promise<EnergyHistory>
members.doc:
Returns Wall Connector charging history.

Energy values are in watt-hours. This endpoint takes no `period`.

members.name: setBackupReserve
members.signature: setBackupReserve(siteId: number | string, percent: number, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergyCommandResult>
members.doc: Sets the reserve held back for grid outages.
params: percent - Reserve level from 0 to 100.

members.name: setOperationMode
members.signature: setOperationMode(siteId: number | string, mode: SiteOperationMode, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergyCommandResult>

members.name: setStormMode
members.signature: setStormMode(siteId: number | string, enabled: boolean, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergyCommandResult>

members.name: setOffGridVehicleChargingReserve
members.signature: setOffGridVehicleChargingReserve(siteId: number | string, percent: number, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergyCommandResult>

members.name: setTimeOfUseSettings
members.signature: setTimeOfUseSettings(siteId: number | string, tariff: Record<string, unknown>, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<EnergyCommandResult>
members.doc:
Configures the utility rate plan used for time-of-use optimization.

The tariff must define at least one season, cover every time period
without gaps or overlaps, and use non-negative prices. Tesla publishes a
worked example alongside the endpoint documentation.
params: tariff - Tariff structure sent as `tou_settings.tariff_content_v2`.

namespaces.blurb: Charging history, sessions, and PDF invoices.
namespaces.name: ChargingResource
namespaces.doc:
Charging history and invoices for the authenticated account.

Accessed as `client.charging`.

members.name: sessions
members.doc:
Returns session detail including pricing and energy.

Available only to business accounts that own a fleet of vehicles.

members.name: invoice
members.doc: Downloads the PDF invoice for a charging event.
params: invoiceId - Invoice identifier taken from a history entry.
members.returns: Raw PDF bytes, not a parsed object.

namespaces.name: TelemetryResource
namespaces.doc:
Fleet Telemetry configuration endpoints.

Accessed as `client.telemetry`.

members.name: createConfig
members.signature: createConfig(vins: string[], config: TelemetryConfig, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<TelemetryConfigResult>
members.doc:
Applies a telemetry configuration to a set of vehicles.

Send this through a Vehicle Command Proxy so the payload is signed. A
vehicle accepts configurations from at most five applications.
params: vins - Vehicles to configure.
config - Server address and the fields to stream.

members.name: createConfigJws
members.doc:
Applies a pre-signed configuration token.

Prefer createConfig through the proxy; this endpoint exists for
callers that sign the JWS themselves using Schnorr over NIST P-256 and
SHA-256.

members.name: deleteConfig
members.doc:
Removes a vehicle's telemetry configuration.

A partner token removes the configuration from any vehicle; a third-party
token is limited to vehicles it has been granted access to.

namespaces.name: PartnerResource
namespaces.doc:
Partner account endpoints.

Accessed as `client.partner`. Every endpoint here requires a partner token
obtained through the `client_credentials` grant; a third-party user token is
rejected.

members.name: register
members.doc:
Registers the application in the current region.

Must be completed once per region before third-party tokens issued for
that region are accepted. Before calling, a PEM-encoded secp256r1 public
key must be reachable at PUBLIC_KEY_PATH on the application
domain, and must remain hosted there for pairing to keep working.
params:
domain - Domain hosting the public key. Must share a root domain
with an allowed origin configured on developer.tesla.com, and is shown to
users during virtual key pairing.

members.name: publicKey
members.doc:
Returns the public key registered for a domain.

A successful response confirms that register completed.
params: domain - Domain to look up. Defaults to the registered domain.

namespaces.blurb: Specs, options, pricing, warranty, and eligibility.
namespaces.name: FleetResource
namespaces.doc:
Vehicle product information and enterprise management.

Accessed as `client.fleet`.

members.name: pricing
members.signature: pricing(request: PricingRequest, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
members.doc:
Returns pricing for a vehicle model in a market.

Requires the `vehicle_pricing_info` scope, which is available only to
partner tokens.

members.name: setEnterprisePayer
members.signature: setEnterprisePayer(vin: string, payer: Record<string, unknown>, options?: RequestOverrides): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>
members.doc:
Sets payer roles for a vehicle.

Requires the `enterprise_management` scope.

namespaces.blurb: Account profile, region discovery, and orders.
namespaces.name: UserResource
namespaces.doc:
Account profile, region, and order endpoints.

Accessed as `client.user`. These endpoints require a user context and are
therefore unavailable to third-party business tokens.

members.name: region
members.doc:
Returns the region serving this account and its Fleet API base URL.

Authoritative, and preferable to inferring a region from a country code
with regionForCountry. Takes no parameters: the result is derived
from the token subject.

namespaces.blurb: Tesla Charging API locations and tariffs (OCPI 2.2.1).
namespaces.name: OcpiResource
namespaces.doc:
Tesla Charging API (OCPI 2.2.1) endpoints.

Accessed as `client.ocpi`. Requires a client constructed with an OCPI token
and the OCPI base URL supplied by Tesla during the credentials handshake.

members.name: locations
members.doc:
Lists charging locations visible to the configured scope.

Results are paged; combine `offset` and `limit`, or use
listAllLocations to iterate.

members.name: listAllLocations
members.doc: Iterates every location, requesting pages lazily.
params: options - Paging controls; `limit` sets the page size.

members.name: credentials
members.doc:
Returns the credentials currently registered for this connection.

Part of the OCPI credentials handshake, which is initiated from the Tesla
developer portal with a `CREDENTIALS_TOKEN_A`.

namespaces.name: OAuthClient
namespaces.doc:
Token acquisition and renewal against the Tesla identity service.

A single instance is safe to share across concurrent requests: overlapping
refreshes collapse into one network call.

members.name: authorizeUrl
members.doc: Builds the URL that a user visits to grant access.
members.returns: An absolute authorization URL to redirect the user to.

members.name: exchangeCode
members.doc: Exchanges an authorization code for tokens and persists them to the store.
throws: {AuthenticationError} When the code is invalid or already used.

members.name: clientCredentials
members.doc:
Obtains a partner token via the `client_credentials` grant.

Partner tokens represent the application itself rather than a user. They
are required for every partner endpoint, including registration, and for
the `vehicle_specs` and `vehicle_pricing_info` scopes.
params: scopes - Scopes to request.

members.name: businessToken
members.doc:
Obtains a third-party business token.

Uses the `client_credentials` grant with the authorization code that a
business administrator generates from the Consent Management page in Tesla
for Business. The resulting token carries no user context, so the
endpoints under `client.user` are unavailable to it.
params: authCode - Authorization code from Consent Management.
scopes - Scopes granted by the business.

members.name: refresh
members.doc:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new token set.

Concurrent calls share a single in-flight request, so a burst of expired
requests triggers only one refresh.
params: refreshToken - Overrides the refresh token held in the store.

members.name: getAccessToken
members.doc:
Returns a valid access token, refreshing it when it is expired or within
the expiry skew window.
members.returns: The access token, or `undefined` when no credentials are stored.

errors.name: TeslaError
errors.doc: Base class for every error thrown by this SDK.

errors.name: PermissionError
errors.doc:
Thrown on HTTP 403 when the token lacks a required scope or the account
lacks access to the requested resource.

errors.name: SigningRequiredError
errors.doc:
Thrown when a command requires Vehicle Command Protocol signing.

Vehicles from 2021 onward reject unsigned commands. Route requests through a
Vehicle Command Proxy by setting the client `baseUrl` to the proxy address.

errors.name: VehicleAsleepError
errors.doc:
Thrown on HTTP 408 when the vehicle is asleep or outside network coverage.

Recoverable by calling VehiclesResource.wakeUp and retrying. The SDK
never wakes a vehicle implicitly, because waking consumes battery charge.

shapes.name: FetchLike
shapes.doc:
Minimal `fetch` signature accepted by the client, allowing a custom
implementation to be injected for testing or for runtime-specific agents.

fields.name: query
fields.type: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined | null>

fields.name: responseType
fields.doc:
How to decode the response body.

`json` parses JSON and falls back to text for other content types.
`binary` returns an `ArrayBuffer` unchanged, which is required for
endpoints such as PDF invoices where text decoding would corrupt bytes.

fields.name: idempotent
fields.doc:
Whether the request may be retried. Defaults to `true` for `GET`.
Non-idempotent commands such as `honk_horn` set this to `false` so a
retry cannot trigger a duplicate physical action.

fields.name: getAuthHeader
fields.doc:
Supplies the `Authorization` header value, refreshing the access token
when required. Omit for unauthenticated clients.

shapes.name: Scope
shapes.definition: /** Allows customers to sign in with their Tesla credentials. */
shapes.doc:
OAuth scopes accepted by Fleet API.

`openid` and `offline_access` are required to receive an id token and a
refresh token respectively.

shapes.name: TokenStore
shapes.doc:
Persistence adapter for tokens.

Implementations may be synchronous or asynchronous, allowing an in-memory
map, `localStorage`, a KV namespace, or a database row to be used
interchangeably.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.doc:
Application secret. Omit for public clients using PKCE, such as browser
and mobile applications, where a secret cannot be kept confidential.

shapes.name: FleetResponse
shapes.doc:
Envelope wrapping every Fleet API payload.

The SDK unwraps this before returning, so `response` is not visible on
resource method return types.

shapes.name: DriveState
shapes.doc:
Drive state subtree of VehicleData.

Location fields require the `vehicle_location` scope and are absent
otherwise.

shapes.name: VehicleDataEndpoint
shapes.doc:
Data subtrees selectable via the `endpoints` query parameter.

Requesting only the needed subtrees reduces payload size and vehicle wake
time.

fields.name: idempotent
fields.doc:
Whether the command may be retried after a transient failure.

Left `false` for commands with a visible physical effect, where a retry
could double-actuate.

fields.name: throwOnFailure
fields.doc: Throw a TeslaError when the vehicle returns `result: false`.

shapes.name: EnergyCommandResult
shapes.doc:
Acknowledgement returned by energy site setting endpoints.

Tesla returns varying shapes here depending on the setting, so only the
common fields are named.

fields.name: type
fields.doc:
Dimension being charged.

Tesla extends OCPI with `CONGESTION_TIME`, which bills time spent charging
past a state-of-charge threshold.

shapes.name: TelemetryFieldConfig
shapes.doc:
Per-field streaming rules.

A value is sent only once `interval_seconds` has elapsed since its last
emission and the value has actually changed, so a short interval does not by
itself increase traffic for a stable signal.

fields.name: minimum_delta
fields.doc:
Minimum change required before the field is re-sent. Location deltas are
measured in meters. Requires firmware 2025.2.6 or later.

fields.name: include_fields
fields.doc:
Fields to include in the same payload whenever this field publishes, even
if their own value has not changed. Requires Fleet Telemetry client 1.3.0.

fields.name: delivery_policy
fields.doc:
Set to `latest` to have the vehicle resend data the server has not
acknowledged. Requires Fleet Telemetry server 0.7.1 or later.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.doc:
Subtrees to fetch. Requesting only what is needed reduces payload size and
shortens how long the vehicle stays awake.

fields.name: vehicle_command_protocol_required
fields.doc:
Whether the vehicle rejects unsigned commands.

When `true`, route commands through a Vehicle Command Proxy.

shapes.name: TeslaClientOptions
shapes.doc:
Configuration for TeslaClient.

Optional properties accept an explicit `undefined` so that values read
straight from `process.env` can be passed without narrowing.

fields.name: region
fields.doc:
Region to route requests to.

A token minted for one region is rejected by the others.

fields.name: baseUrl
fields.doc:
Overrides the base URL derived from `region`.

Set this to the address of a Vehicle Command Proxy so that commands are
signed, or to a mock server in tests.

fields.name: accessToken
fields.doc:
A static access token.

Convenient for scripts. Provide `tokens` or a `tokenStore` instead when
the client should refresh credentials on its own.

fields.name: tokenStore
fields.doc: Persistence for tokens. Required for automatic refresh across restarts.

fields.name: ocpiToken
fields.doc:
OCPI credentials token for the Tesla Charging API.

The Charging API is a separate product from the Fleet API charging
endpoints under `client.charging`: it exposes Tesla's public network as a
CPO and authenticates with OCPI's `Token` scheme rather than OAuth.

Setting this affects only the `ocpi` namespace, which is given its own
transport. Fleet API calls on the same client continue to use the OAuth
session, so one instance can serve both products.

fields.name: ocpiBaseUrl
fields.doc:
Base URL for the Charging API, supplied by Tesla during the OCPI
credentials handshake.

Defaults to `baseUrl`, then to the region host. Set it whenever the
Charging API is served from a different origin than Fleet API.

fields.name: timeoutMs
fields.doc: Request timeout in milliseconds.

fields.name: fetch
fields.doc: `fetch` implementation to use.

fields.name: userAgent
fields.doc: Value sent as `User-Agent` off-browser.

shapes.name: TeslaErrorCode
shapes.doc:
Stable discriminant for TeslaError.code.

Values are part of the public API and will not change within a major version.
